A1.justification: Both complete 28-page PDFs describe the same WinDiNet research. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite layout changes and reference renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original surrogate benchmarks, VAE ablations, CFD-verified layout optimization, and generalization experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds pretraining controls and quantitative comparisons on real-city footprints.

M1.justification: The LTX-Video backbone, conditioning, VAE adaptation, physics losses, and differentiable layout optimization remain unchanged. Training from scratch is introduced as an experimental control, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic urban layouts, the same four real cities, single- and multi-inlet optimization, and the same extrapolation scenarios. The new real-city table quantifies existing coverage rather than introducing another domain or task.

E2.justification: v3 Table 8 adds RNO, OFormer, Poseidon, AFNO, FNO, and U-Net comparisons to the real-city experiment, where v1 presented only WinDiNet predictions. These six methods already appear in both versions' main benchmark.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds compute-matched controls removing DiT pretraining and both DiT/VAE pretraining. Table 8 introduces quantitative evaluation at 15 m/s on four cities with eight augmentations each. The original 10,000/1,000/2,000 data split and established evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted ablation isolating the contribution of pretraining and quantitative evidence for the previously qualitative real-city generalization study. Existing VAE, extrapolation, channel-assignment, and inverse-optimization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 8 averages augmented test cases; it does not introduce repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and inverse-design scores are unchanged. The new pretraining ablation reports VRMSE 0.57 and 0.92 versus 0.52 for the pretrained configuration. New real-city results include WinDiNet VRMSE 0.683 versus RNO 0.803, while AFNO achieves the lowest W1 at 2.511.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, including Equations 1–17, physics penalties, rasterization, and optimization regularizers, is retained. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain pretrained-video adaptation for accurate wind prediction and differentiable urban-layout optimization. The abstract's change from 10,000 simulations to a 13,000-simulation dataset reflects the already documented total dataset, without expanding the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes a substantial part of accuracy to pretraining based on the scratch controls. The conclusion adds learned solution priors from generative inverse-design methods as a complementary direction. Existing limitations and generalization interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises code, weights, and data upon publication; v3 supplies a repository address for code and weights and offers data upon request. Section 4.5 newly specifies FP16 and an inference memory requirement within 24 GB, without establishing a changed inference procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds CinDM and DiffPhyCon as complementary generative inverse-design approaches in the conclusion. Most other bibliography changes concern metadata and numbering of existing works, rather than a changed research position.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized prose additions, abstract wording, revised acknowledgments, bibliographic editing, and small corrections, including removal of the mismatched morph-mode description near Figure 11. The section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds real-city Table 8, renumbers the channel-assignment table to Table 9, and relocates or resizes several retained figures. Captions and labels receive small edits. New Table 8 incorrectly bolds RNO's W1 value despite AFNO having a lower value.

improvement.justification: The compute-matched pretraining controls strengthen the central transfer-learning argument, and Table 8 extends v1's qualitative real-city evidence with numerical baseline comparisons. Access instructions and precision/memory details improve reproducibility information. These targeted gains outweigh the table's incorrect W1 highlighting, although augmentation details and statistical uncertainty remain unreported and dataset access is by request.
